text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Import revenues have decreased from mid-November as the importers have stopped getting their goods cleared.
- Government is considering abolishing regulatory duties on imports.
- Iran has s offered Pakistan to assist in construction of roads and bridges in rural areas.

- A three-member team led by prime minister's Advisor on Finance, Planning and Economic Affairs Shahid Javed Burki left on Saturday for the United Arab Emirates to negotiate $250 million loan for improving balance of payment position.
- Five out of the six subsidiaries of Pakistan International Airlines have suffered a record loss of 272 million rupees ($6.7 million).
- The Lahore Stock Exchange has started computerised trading on Saturday.
- Two Indian organisations -- State trading Corporation and Sugar General Imports and Exports Corporation -- are in the run for getting 50,000 tonnes sugar tender from Pakistan.
- One of the two pre-inspection companies has threatened to go to the court if the government cancelled its license.
- Caretaker prime minister Meraj Khalid has said his government has failed in holding the accountability of corrupt people because of loop-holes in the laws.
- The second tranche of $76 million would be released after the International Monetary Fund (IMF) receives the financial data for December and finds it satisfactory.
